t.E234.agn: In 2017, using new toxicological data, EFSA set the acceptable daily intake (ADI) at 1 mg nisin A/kg body weight and concluded that the proposed extension of use in unripened cheese and heat-treated meat products would not raise a safety concern.
t.E234.body: Nisin is a small protein (peptide) and is broken down by digestive enzymes.
t.E234.prod: Produced by fermentation with lactic acid bacteria (Streptococcus lactis).
t.E234.regx.0: ADI 1 mg nisin A/kg body weight/day (raised from 0.13 mg/kg in 2006); no safety concern for the proposed extension of use.
t.E234.summary: A natural antimicrobial peptide produced by bacteria through fermentation. It prevents bacterial growth in processed cheese, puddings and canned foods.
t.E234.what: It is a preservative produced by fermentation that inhibits the growth of certain bacteria.
